weekly_visit_frequency.label: Weekly visit frequency
weekly_visit_frequency.concern: More visits are billed each week than the benign-profile cases show.
weekly_visit_frequency.benign: The plan of care may call for this frequency, for example help every morning and evening.
weekly_visit_frequency.step: Compare billed visits with the plan of care.
weekly_visit_frequency.records: Plan of care and the provider's visit record for the billed period.
weekly_visit_frequency.if_clean: Billed visits match the plan of care.
weekly_visit_frequency.if_not: Billed visits exceed the plan of care or cannot be evidenced.

residential.benign: The count may include services billed separately from the daily rate, such as therapy sessions.
residential.step: Compare billed days with the residency record and list any separately billed services.
residential.records: Itemised facility statement and residency record for the billed period.
residential.if_clean: Billed days match the residency record and the extra units are separately listed services.
residential.if_not: More days are billed than the resident was there, or the units cannot be evidenced.

day_centre.benign: Some centres open at weekends, and the count may include transport billed per trip.
day_centre.step: Compare billed attendances with the centre's sign-in sheets and opening days.
day_centre.records: Attendance (sign-in) sheets and the centre's opening days for the billed period.
day_centre.if_clean: Billed attendances match the sign-in sheets.
day_centre.if_not: Attendances are billed for days the member was not signed in or the centre was closed.

member_provider_distance_miles.label: Member-provider distance
member_provider_distance_miles.concern: The provider is a long way from the member for in-person care.
member_provider_distance_miles.benign: The address may be an agency office rather than the caregiver's base, or the member may have moved.
member_provider_distance_miles.step: Confirm where care was delivered and where the caregiver travelled from.
member_provider_distance_miles.records: Place of service, the caregiver's base, and the member's address history.
member_provider_distance_miles.if_clean: Care was delivered close to the member (an office address, or a move).
member_provider_distance_miles.if_not: Nobody can show who travelled to deliver the care.

residential.benign: The address on file may be the insured's former home or a relative's, not the facility.
residential.step: Confirm the admission date and which address is on file for the insured.
residential.records: Admission record and the insured's address history.
residential.if_clean: The address on file is a former home or a relative's; the insured lives at the facility.
residential.if_not: Nobody can show that the insured lives at the facility.

day_centre.benign: Centres often run transport or a relative drives, and the address on file may be out of date.
day_centre.step: Confirm how the member gets to the centre and which address is on file.
day_centre.records: Transport log or sign-in sheets, and the member's address history.
day_centre.if_clean: Transport or a current address explains the distance.
day_centre.if_not: Nobody can show how the member reached the centre on billed days.

prior_claims_last_12mo.label: Prior claims, last 12 months
prior_claims_last_12mo.concern: Claim activity is more frequent than the benign-profile cases show.
prior_claims_last_12mo.benign: An ongoing LTC claim is usually invoiced monthly, so up to 12 a year can be routine.
prior_claims_last_12mo.step: Review the 12-month claim history for a step change in frequency.
prior_claims_last_12mo.records: Claim history with service periods and payment status.
prior_claims_last_12mo.if_clean: Claims follow a regular invoicing rhythm.
prior_claims_last_12mo.if_not: Claim frequency jumped without a change in care needs.

weekend_billing_ratio.label: Weekend billing share
weekend_billing_ratio.concern: A large share of billing falls on weekends.
weekend_billing_ratio.benign: Care delivered every day of the week puts about 0.29 (2 days in 7) on weekends.
weekend_billing_ratio.step: Check that weekend service dates match scheduled care or opening days.
weekend_billing_ratio.if_clean: Weekend dates match scheduled care or opening days.
weekend_billing_ratio.if_not: Weekend billing does not match when care is delivered.

amount_vs_peer_avg_pct.label: Amount vs peer average
amount_vs_peer_avg_pct.concern: The claim is well above the peer average.
amount_vs_peer_avg_pct.benign: Higher care needs, more hours of care or a costlier area can explain it.
amount_vs_peer_avg_pct.step: Confirm the peer group and the hours or days of care behind the amount.
amount_vs_peer_avg_pct.records: Peer-group definition; itemised statement with hours or days and the rate charged.
amount_vs_peer_avg_pct.if_clean: More hours of care or a higher-cost area explain the amount.
amount_vs_peer_avg_pct.if_not: The amount cannot be tied to hours or days of care.

round_dollar_billing_ratio.label: Round-dollar billing share
round_dollar_billing_ratio.concern: Many invoices are round amounts, which hours x hourly rate rarely produces.
round_dollar_billing_ratio.benign: Flat daily or monthly charges are round by nature.
round_dollar_billing_ratio.step: Check invoice amounts against the provider's stated rate x hours or days.
round_dollar_billing_ratio.records: Itemised invoices with hours or days, and the provider's rate sheet.
round_dollar_billing_ratio.if_clean: Amounts follow a flat daily or monthly charge.
round_dollar_billing_ratio.if_not: Amounts have no rate x time basis.

duplicate_service_billed.label: Duplicate service billed
duplicate_service_billed.concern: The same service appears to have been billed more than once.
duplicate_service_billed.benign: One line may be a corrected resubmission, or a reversal and rebill.
duplicate_service_billed.step: Look for a reversal-and-rebill pair behind the duplicate line.
duplicate_service_billed.records: Claim-line history with adjustment and reversal codes.
duplicate_service_billed.if_clean: The second line is a corrected resubmission or a reversal and rebill.
duplicate_service_billed.if_not: The same service was paid more than once.

shared_contact_with_provider.label: Shared contact with provider
shared_contact_with_provider.concern: Member and provider share an address, phone, e-mail or bank detail.
shared_contact_with_provider.benign: It may be a facility address, or a relative who helps with paperwork. If a relative is the paid caregiver, whether that is payable is a coverage question for the examiner.
shared_contact_with_provider.step: Find out which contact field matched (address, phone, e-mail or bank) and whose it is.
shared_contact_with_provider.records: The matched contact field and its history; provider ownership.
shared_contact_with_provider.if_clean: The match is a facility address or a relative who helps with paperwork.
shared_contact_with_provider.if_not: A bank or phone detail belongs to the provider.

recent_policy_change_flag.label: Recent policy change
recent_policy_change_flag.concern: The policy record changed shortly before this claim activity. Payee, bank or power-of-attorney changes matter most, and the insured may be the one being exploited.
recent_policy_change_flag.benign: Routine updates, such as a new mailing address after a move, are common.
recent_policy_change_flag.step: Pull the policy change log: what changed, who asked, when and through which channel.
recent_policy_change_flag.records: Policy change log with requester and channel.
recent_policy_change_flag.if_clean: A routine update requested by the insured or a known representative.
recent_policy_change_flag.if_not: A payee, bank or power-of-attorney change redirected payments.

service_overlap_other_provider.label: Service overlap with another provider
service_overlap_other_provider.concern: Two providers billed for overlapping time.
service_overlap_other_provider.benign: Some services legitimately run together, or providers were changing over.
service_overlap_other_provider.step: Line up both providers' visit times for the overlapping dates.
service_overlap_other_provider.records: Both providers' visit records with times.
service_overlap_other_provider.if_clean: The two providers' visits fall at different times or are complementary.
service_overlap_other_provider.if_not: Both providers billed the same hours.

residential.benign: A resident can receive extra services from an outside provider, such as private-duty care or therapy, on days the facility also bills.
residential.step: Line up the facility's billed days with the other provider's dates and what each delivered.
residential.records: Both providers' statements with dates and services.
residential.if_clean: The second provider delivered a service the facility's charge does not include.
residential.if_not: Both providers billed the same care for the same days.

day_centre.benign: Home care before or after centre hours on the same day is common.
day_centre.step: Line up centre attendance hours with the other provider's visit times.
day_centre.if_clean: The home care fell outside the centre's hours.
